name: Messenger RNA (mRNA) Replacement Therapy
therapeuticGoalDescription: Restore functional protein expression by delivering synthetic mRNA encoding the therapeutic protein.
molecularDefect: Loss-of-function mutations, haploinsufficiency, absent or severely reduced protein production where transient protein replacement is therapeutically beneficial.
diseaseMechanism: Exogenous mRNA is delivered into the cytoplasm, translated by host ribosomes into the therapeutic protein, thereby restoring or supplementing endogenous protein function without altering genomic DNA.
suitableVariantTypes: Nonsense mutations; frameshift mutations; deletions; loss-of-function variants; haploinsufficiency; null alleles.
typicalDiseases: Propionic acidemia; Methylmalonic acidemia; Cystic fibrosis (experimental); Ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency; Infectious diseases (vaccines).
rnaTargetRegion: None. The therapeutic mRNA itself is delivered rather than targeting endogenous RNA.
transcriptRequirement: None. Expression is independent of endogenous transcript production.
typicalLength: Approximately 1–5 kb, depending on the encoded protein.
designRules: Optimize codon usage; select appropriate untranslated regions (UTRs); include 5′ cap, poly(A) tail, and modified nucleosides to enhance stability and reduce innate immune activation; validate protein expression.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Optimized to promote efficient translation while maintaining mRNA stability.
offTargetConsiderations: Innate immune activation; transient expression; delivery-related toxicity; excessive protein expression.
advantages: No genomic integration; rapid protein expression; adaptable platform; suitable for repeated dosing.
limitations: Transient expression; requires efficient delivery; storage and stability challenges; repeated administration often necessary.
fdaApprovedDrugs: None. No mRNA protein replacement therapy has been approved. The approved mRNA products (Comirnaty, Spikevax) are prophylactic vaccines — mRNA encoding a pathogen antigen to raise an immune response — which is a different indication class and does not evidence protein replacement.
clinicalTrialExamples: Multiple clinical programs in infectious diseases, rare diseases, and oncology.

evidenceLevel.note: Downgraded from 'Very High'. The previous rating rested on the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, which are not protein replacement therapies. Evidence for the replacement indication is clinical-stage only (propionic acidemia, methylmalonic acidemia, OTC deficiency).

references.paper: Katalin Karikó et al. Suppression of RNA recognition by Toll-like receptors: the impact of nucleoside modification.
Drew Weissman & Katalin Karikó reviews on mRNA therapeutics

arbitration.flagReason: No approved mRNA protein replacement therapy exists, so a stated applicability for this mechanism could not be checked against any case in the world. Surfaced qualitatively instead of scored.
